newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks sink to month low by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks sink to month low by close.

text.p: *Stocks end down as profit takers cash in on light volume, weak dollar dampens rate cut hopes. Volume 290.91 million, A$709.80 million, 1,070 stocks traded, 273 steady, 248 up, 549 down.
The Australian share market sank to its lowest close since June 12 on Tuesday with profit takers moving in as hopes of an imminent interest rate cut were dampened by the weak Australian dollar.
The All Ordinaries index shed 35.4 points to 2,637.6, touching bottom late in the day at 2,632.1.
September share price index futures contracts were down 29 points at 2,644, a 6.4 point premium to the underlying index, in active trade with 11,552 contracts traded.
The soft tone from Monday spilled over, the selling continuing on light volume yet again.
"It's very much a repeat of yesterday -- there is not great business but it's all on the sell side," said a Sydney broker.
The most compelling reason for the weakness seemed to be the dashed hopes of a quick rate cut in the face of the falling Australian dollar.

"That is the conventional wisdom in any case and the market is sliding as a result," said head of equities at Intersuisse, Andrew Sekely, although he noted the selling was not confined to the interest rate-sensitive sectors.
"Not withstanding that, the metals stocks, which should be helped by the soft Aussie dollar, are not doing much at all."

The interest rate sensitive sectors were hardest hit on the day, with the banking index shedding nearly two percent and the building materials index diving over three percent compared to an overall market loss of 1.3 percent.
Among the building materials stocks, Boral and CSR were hit hardest, both losing nearly five percent to A$4.06 and A$4.82 respectively.
In the banks, National Australia, which makes up about 34 percent of the sector benchmark, fell 2.2 percent to A$19.168, while Westpac fell 3.3 percent to A$7.67.
Other losses were broadly spread, albeit at reduced levels.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to four, while about 26 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bond yields touched their highest level in a week just before the close, fuelled by comments by a government minister, which raised concerns over future wages growth. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.74 percent, compared to Monday's 6.67 percent.
Persistent speculative and technical selling knocked the Australian dollar down to fresh 18-month lows on Tuesday, a pattern which was threatening to become routine.
By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), the local currency was hovering at US$0.7360/65 having slipped from US$0.7375/80 here Monday and US$0.7445/50 late last week.
